content.comment_body: Hello, I'm attempting to connect two [product_name] devices using a switch, which then connects to a router and the internet. When I try to manually set the IP address via TCP/IPv4, I'm unable to communicate with either device. If TCP/IPv4 is set to automatic, both devices are visible, but I can only upload the program to one. I refresh the list of accessible devices before transferring the program. One uses IP 192.168.0.3 and works properly; the other uses 192.168.0.2 and gives an 'Unable to access remote device' error. Both devices have the same subnet mask (255.255.255.0) and gateway (192.168.0.1). Direct connection to the PC with a cable allows uploading to both. I'm not an administrator, so I can't adjust router settings. The devices are [version_no] FS:04 and I have [product_name] version 8.1.
Hello, What is your PC's IP address?
Hello, The PC's IP address is 192.168.0.27.
Does your computer have the same gateway and subnet mask, and are you able to ping the devices? Have you tried unplugging them?

Subnet and gateway match those assigned to the devices. Ping results have been attached. I tried unplugging and reconnecting, but only 192.168.0.3 responds. 0.2 remains unreachable even when 0.3 is not connected to the switch.
After unplugging and reconnecting the cable from switch to router, I can now upload programs to both devices. Next, I'll prepare a program to test further.

analysis.insight_summary: The user had trouble uploading programs to two [product_name] devices on a shared network, where only direct cable connection worked for both. Over the network, only one was accessible at a time, with the other giving a remote access error. The problem was resolved after unplugging and plugging back the switch-to-router connection, enabling normal access to both devices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to reliably communicate with and upload programs to both [product_name] devices over the network from their PC, with consistent visibility and access to multiple devices using the same network setup.
